questioned.title: Overriding vfuncFinalize makes GTKX re-reference the instance while GObject is finalizing it, emitting GLib criticals and aborting
questioned.rootCause: The vtable trampoline marshalled the instance argument of every class slot through the ordinary tracked object path. For an overridden `ObjectClass.finalize`, that path ran while GObject was already finalizing the instance: `acquire_decoded_ref` in packages/native/src/ffi/codec/object.rs took `g_object_ref` on an object whose refcount had reached zero (critical 1), `wrapper::wrapper_value` found nothing because the wrapper's own cleanup had just deleted the napi reference and removed its toggle reference, so a fresh `External<Handle>` reached JavaScript, where `getOrCreateWrapper` built a new wrapper and called `registerWrapper` into `set_wrapper`, which `g_object_ref_sink`ed (critical 2), `g_object_add_toggle_ref`ed (critical 3) and unreffed twice (criticals 4 and 5). Five GLib criticals per finalized instance, and a SIGABRT under the `G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals` that @gtkx/vitest sets. The same mechanism applies to `ObjectClass.dispose`, where the new toggle reference resurrects the object mid-teardown instead of tripping an assertion.
questioned.reviewAssessment:
The mechanism the fix introduces is right, but the trigger that turns it on is keyed to the wrong thing, so the fix covers only a minority of the reported defect and the regression test happens to sit inside exactly that minority.

packages/runtime/src/register-class.ts gates the new marking on a literal string set:

    const TEARDOWN_SLOTS: Set<string> = new Set(["ObjectClass.dispose", "ObjectClass.finalize"]);
    ...
    if (!TEARDOWN_SLOTS.has(`${descriptor.className}.${descriptor.vfuncName}`)) return descriptor.argDescriptors;

`descriptor.className` is the GIR type-struct name of whichever ancestor registry `findClassVfuncDescriptor` (packages/runtime/src/vfunc.ts:7) reaches first while walking the class chain. The generated store emits the teardown slots on TWO class structs, not one: node_modules/.gtkx/gi/gobject/gobject.js:7959/7965 carry `className: "ObjectClass"`, and lines 8022/8029 carry `className: "InitiallyUnownedClass"`. Neither gtk.js nor adw.js declares `vfuncDispose`/`vfuncFinalize` at all, and node_modules/.gtkx/gi/gtk/gtk.js:9041 is `export class Widget extends GObject.InitiallyUnowned`. So every widget subclass, and every direct GInitiallyUnowned subclass, resolves the slot to `InitiallyUnownedClass.finalize` / `InitiallyUnownedClass.dispose`, which the set misses, and the instance argument goes down the unchanged tracked path.

Measured against the committed build (packages/native/native.linux-x64-gnu.node and packages/runtime/dist both contain the fix): a subclass of `GObject.InitiallyUnowned` overriding `vfuncFinalize` still prints the same five criticals in the same order the record documents, and still exits 134 under G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals. The identical file with `extends GObject` is clean. `vfuncDispose` on an InitiallyUnowned subclass runs twice, which is the mid-teardown resurrection the commit message claims to have closed. The defect record listed the Gtk.Box subclass (probes/finalize-natural-gc.ts) as part of this same finding, so the widget case is in scope, and it is also the case the subclassing guide steers users toward.

The regression test at packages/e2e/tests/runtime/finalize-vfunc.test.ts uses `extends GObject`, the one base class the fix reaches. It passes now (1 passed, 418ms) and it genuinely would fail without the change: the InitiallyUnowned probe is that same code path with the marking absent, and it aborts the process, which under vitest.config.base.ts:22 (`G_DEBUG: "fatal-criticals"`) surfaces as a dead worker. But the test cannot detect the hole it leaves, and there is no test for `vfuncDispose` at all despite the summary claiming that slot is covered.

Nothing else breaks. `is_call_scoped` is `Option<bool>` in packages/native/src/ffi/descriptor.rs so every existing JS descriptor deserializes to false, all `ObjectCodec` / `Descriptor::Object` construction sites in packages/native are updated, `Handle::borrowed_gobject` is a distinct kind from `from_glib_borrow` so `as_gobject_ptr`, `take_owned`, `get_wrapper` and `get_type` all stay correct with `owned: None`, and `wrapCallScopedObject` is reachable only from the new descriptor flag. `getOrCreateWrapper` and the call-scoped variant genuinely share one lookup-create-bind path in packages/runtime/src/registry.ts, so no dead branch was left behind, except in the sense that the whole pre-fix path stays live for every teardown slot the string set fails to name.

No convention violations found: no inline exports, sections stay ordered, exports contiguous and naturally sorted, no `!`, no `as unknown as`, no `readonly`, no prose comments in TypeScript, boolean named `isCallScoped`, and `existingWrapperFor` fits the `<noun>For` table-lookup rule.

The narrower and correct fix is to stop keying on the GIR struct name. packages/codegen/src/store/gi/vtable.ts:76-81 already enumerates `vfuncDispose` and `vfuncFinalize` in UNCALLABLE_SLOT_KEYS while emitting each vtable, so setting the flag there marks ObjectClass, InitiallyUnownedClass and any future re-declaration in one place, with no runtime string table to drift. Failing that, key the runtime set on `descriptor.vfuncName` alone, restricted to an arg 0 whose `kind` is `"object"`, which picks up InitiallyUnownedClass and correctly skips `ParamSpecClass.finalize` (its arg 0 is a GParamSpec fundamental).
reviewProblems: Incomplete fix: TEARDOWN_SLOTS in packages/runtime/src/register-class.ts:169 names only 'ObjectClass.dispose' and 'ObjectClass.finalize', but the generated store also emits those slots as 'InitiallyUnownedClass.dispose' and 'InitiallyUnownedClass.finalize' (node_modules/.gtkx/gi/gobject/gobject.js:8022 and :8029). Since Gtk.Widget extends GObject.InitiallyUnowned and no Gtk/Adw class declares the slots, every widget subclass and every InitiallyUnowned subclass still takes the old tracked path.

Reproduced against the committed build: a class extending GObject.InitiallyUnowned that overrides vfuncFinalize still emits the exact five reported criticals (object_ref '!object_already_finalized', g_object_ref_sink, g_object_add_toggle_ref, two g_object_unref) and still exits 134 under G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals. The same file with 'extends GObject' is clean, proving the flag, not the environment, is the difference.
The dispose half is also unfixed on that path: a vfuncDispose override on an InitiallyUnowned subclass runs twice, which is the mid-teardown resurrection the commit claims to have closed.

The regression test packages/e2e/tests/runtime/finalize-vfunc.test.ts subclasses GObject, the single base class the fix reaches, so it locks in the partial fix and can never catch the widget case that the defect record explicitly listed (probes/finalize-natural-gc.ts, a Gtk.Box subclass). No test covers vfuncDispose at all, though the summary claims the slot is covered.

The gate is a literal string coupling to codegen output with no test asserting that the two names still resolve, so a store change silently reopens the crash. The flag belongs in packages/codegen/src/store/gi/vtable.ts, which already enumerates vfuncDispose/vfuncFinalize in UNCALLABLE_SLOT_KEYS, or should key on descriptor.vfuncName plus an object-kind arg 0.

website/guide/subclassing.md:125 now documents that dispose and finalize always receive a call-scoped receiver. That is false for any subclass below GInitiallyUnowned, which is every widget, so the guide promises behavior the runtime does not deliver for the common case.

markInstanceCallScoped (packages/runtime/src/register-class.ts:456) is a structural clone of markValueCallerAllocated directly above it, differing only in the index constant and the flag name; one markArg(index, patch) helper covers both.

Nothing enforces the call-scoped lifetime the design depends on. The regression test itself pushes `this` and getHandle(this) into arrays that outlive the override, leaving an ExternalObject<Handle> pointing at freed memory; it is inert only because nothing dereferences it, and the test enshrines the escape as expected usage.

questioned.title: A runtime exception in a component during Fast Refresh terminates the whole gtkx dev session
questioned.rootCause: The dev runner had no owner for a render-time or effect-time exception, and it restarted into the module that had just thrown. React 19 handles an uncaught render error by queuing a root error update whose callback invokes onUncaughtError (react-reconciler.development.js:7010 createRootErrorUpdate), so the error is reported only AFTER the commit that has already deleted the tree. That deletion tore down the Gio.Application, whose shutdown signal reached onApplicationShutdown in packages/cli/src/dev/runner.ts; because refreshTracker.isRefreshing() was true it called deps.exit(RESTART_EXIT_CODE) synchronously, before React ever ran its error callback. The error was therefore swallowed, and the supervisor relaunched the runner into the identical broken module. In the relaunched process GTKX's createRoot rethrows through rethrowUncaughtRenderError, so the exception escaped from a scheduler task to Node's default uncaught-exception handler and the process exited 1; supervisor.ts handleChildExit saw a code that is not RESTART_EXIT_CODE and called process.exit(1), taking the Vite server, the file watcher and the whole gtkx dev command down. The same termination happened when the entry module itself failed to evaluate (ReferenceError: Extra is not defined), because run() awaited server.ssrLoadModule(entryPath) with nothing around it, so the rejection propagated out of main() and the bin wrapper exited 1.
questioned.reviewAssessment: The change fixes the reported defect at its cause, not at the symptom: the dev runner now owns application failures (uncaughtException/unhandledRejection listeners, a reconciler error hook registered through the app's own module graph, and a try/catch around the entry load), so a render-time or effect-time throw can no longer escape to Node, and restartAfterRefresh no longer relaunches into the module that just threw. Recovery on the next save is a RESTART_EXIT_CODE restart, matching website/guide/getting-started.md:61. The regression tests are genuine and not tautological: they cannot typecheck against the parent (DevRunnerDeps lacked both new members and waitForApplicationId took one argument), and each of the three decision points is individually pinned (startFailedHarness fires shutdown before the render error, so only the hasFailed re-check in restartAfterRefresh keeps exit uncalled; the next-save test asserts ssrLoadModule is not called again, which only holds via the hasFailed branch in requiresRestart; the failing-entry test rejects ssrLoadModule, which without loadEntry's catch rejects run()). I verified by reading the code rather than reverting; the tree is untouched. pnpm vitest run --project cli packages/cli/tests/dev/ passes 94 tests and eslint on the seven changed files is clean. No CLAUDE.md violation (no inline exports, sections ordered, no comments, no `!`, no `as unknown as`, no `readonly`, allowed boolean prefixes), no legacy path or shim left, and the only production consumer (runner-main.ts) is unaffected. However, the fix treats the failure latch as a permanent property of the session and feeds it from channels that are not all fatal, which introduces two reachable regressions (a boundary-caught error or a stray unhandled rejection permanently disables Fast Refresh and makes a normal window close hang the dev command instead of exiting 0) and leaves the attachApplication exit-1 branch, named in the defect record, still able to take the whole command down.
reviewProblems: An error caught by a React error boundary trips the failure latch. packages/react/src/reconciler/root.ts:82 calls errorHandlerSlot.get()?.(error) inside the onCaughtError wrapper, not only onUncaughtError, so a healthy app whose boundary handled an error prints 'Application error; keeping the dev server up. Fix the error and save again.' and latches hasFailed. createRoot's JSDoc documents boundary-caught errors as supported and packages/testing/src/types.ts:183 exposes onCaughtError publicly.

After any latch, closing the application window no longer stops `gtkx dev`. handleApplicationShutdown (packages/cli/src/dev/runner.ts:190) checks failure.hasFailed() before the quit path, so a normal window close hits parkSession instead of 'Application quit - stopping dev runner...' + closeAndExit. Combined with the permanent process.on('uncaughtException') listener the command never exits and needs Ctrl-C; it exited 0 before.

After any latch, Fast Refresh is permanently replaced by a full process restart. requiresRestart (packages/cli/src/dev/runner.ts:61) returns true unconditionally once hasFailed(), and FailureTracker has no reset, so every subsequent save restarts the process for the rest of the session.

unhandledRejection is routed into the same fatal latch as a render throw. An ordinary async click handler that rejects, or a stray rejection from Vite or the MCP client, now produces the two regressions above in an otherwise healthy application.

The exit-1 branch the defect record named is still live: attachApplication ends in closeAndExit(session, refusedExitCode()) (packages/cli/src/dev/runner.ts:243), which the supervisor turns into process.exit(1), killing the Vite server and watcher, whenever the application fails to register and the failure has not been latched yet. It is guarded only by the preceding hasFailed() check, which races the uncaughtException macrotask.

RESTART_DECISION_DELAY_MS = 0 makes restartAfterRefresh a timing assumption: it re-checks the latch exactly one macrotask after the GTK shutdown signal. If the error lands later, or if ssrLoadModule('@gtkx/react/internal') ever resolves a different module instance than the app's @gtkx/react so only the slower uncaughtException channel fires, the runner restarts needlessly. The unit harness mocks watchRenderErrors, so nothing in the suite proves the two paths share a module instance, and the end-to-end log cannot distinguish them because both channels print the same message.

FailureTracker remembers only the last cause (packages/cli/src/dev/failure-tracker.ts), so an A/B/A sequence reports A twice, contradicting the claim that each distinct cause is reported exactly once.

run() logs 'HMR enabled - watching for changes...' even when the entry failed and the session is parked, directly contradicting the 'fix the error and save again' message printed just above it; a new test pins that behavior.
